concerns.text: T015 (markers.py) explicitly lists a dependency on T003 (config.py) for the keyword dictionary. However, T015 is marked [P] (parallel-safe). If T015 runs before T003 completes, it will fail to load the dictionary. The [P] tag is semantically incorrect here; T015 must be ordered after T003, not parallel to it.

T017 (stats.py) lists a dependency on 'Phase 3' (Generation) logic in its description, yet it is marked [P] (parallel-safe) and placed in Phase 4. While the schema (Phase 2) is ready, the task description implies a need for the generation logic to be functional. If T017 is truly parallel-safe, it should only depend on the schema contract (Phase 2), not the 'Phase 3 logic'. The current phrasing creates a semantic ordering conflict: if it needs Phase 3 logic, it cannot be [P] relative to Phase 3.

T022 (human_rater.py) depends on T021 (rubric.md). T022 is marked [P]. If T022 executes before T021 creates the file, the script will fail. The [P] tag is invalid for a task that consumes an artifact created by another task in the same phase. T022 must be ordered after T021.

T030 (main.py) orchestrates Generation (Phase 3) and Analysis (Phase 4). It is marked [P]. However, T030 cannot run until the logic in Phase 3 and Phase 4 is implemented. While it might be parallel to *other* Phase 7 tasks, it is not parallel to the completion of Phases 3 and 4. The [P] tag is misleading in the context of the full pipeline flow, as it implies it can start immediately alongside the generation/analysis tasks, which is impossible.

Phase 8 tasks (T045-T050) are marked [P] and listed as depending on Phase 6 and Phase 4. However, T050 (Update rubric) depends on the *output* of T045-T049 (the new analysis reports) to update the criteria. T050 is marked [P], implying it can run in parallel with T045-T049, but it semantically requires their results. T050 must be ordered after T045-T049.
